source.rationale:
TWIN CONTRACT. dym-transform and dym-transform-partial are byte-identical apart from the `promotion` DOMAIN_PROBE entry (and two comment rules), so every behaviour that is not promotion-specific MUST hold identically on both. Ported deliberately rather than left to the twin: this repo has been bitten before by a fork asserted to be identical that had quietly drifted, and a rule proven on only one copy is a rule the other copy is free to lose. Same inputs, same expected output as dym-transform/HC-allowed-lookup-is-honoured-by-the-census-too.json — if the two ever disagree, one of these two fixtures fails.

Behaviour under test: The census applies the SAME allowed_lookup filter as the selection, and it must be the allowed types that are counted. Here one code carries two product uuids (genuinely cross-company, so it must be excluded) plus a promotion uuid the lookup forbids. Inverting the census filter would count only the forbidden entry, see a single uuid, and cheerfully probe a code that belongs to two different companies.
